name: Recycling
description: The software project will develop a user-friendly web application that allows users to discover and manage recycling facilities. Key features include searching for nearby centers by zip code, viewing operational hours, accessing maps of recycling locations, and receiving notifications about events. Administrators will manage facility information and user feedback, ensuring data security while enabling communication between facility representatives and site admins to improve community recycling efforts.
rawDescription: The software project will develop a user-friendly web application that allows users to discover and manage recycling facilities. Key features include searching for nearby centers by zip code, viewing operational hours, accessing maps of recycling locations, and receiving notifications about events. Administrators will manage facility information and user feedback, ensuring data security while enabling communication between facility representatives and site admins to improve community recycling efforts.
highLevelGoals: To allow end users to quickly and easily find nearby recycling centers based on their location or other criteria.
To ensure end users can view essential information such as operational hours, accepted materials, and precise locations via maps.
To notify end users about upcoming recycling events, collection drives, or changes in services.
To allow administrators to efficiently add, update, and remove information about recycling facilities, ensuring users always have reliable data.
To provide administrators with tools to review, categorize, and act upon feedback submitted by end-users.
To enable administrators to communicate effectively with facility representatives and other relevant parties to coordinate efforts and resolve issues.
To allow facility representatives to submit and maintain up-to-date details about their recycling center, including services, hours, and contact information.
To enable facility representatives to communicate with administrators regarding operational improvements, event coordination, and community engagement strategies.

baselineCritiques.actors: The identified actors are accurate and cover the main roles described in the text: End Users (who search and manage), Administrators (who manage data and security), and Facility Representatives (who communicate with admins). There are no obvious omissions or contradictions based on the provided description.
baselineCritiques.highLevelGoals: The high-level goals are well-aligned with the software description and actors. They correctly cover the core functionalities: discovery (search by zip code), information access (hours, maps), notifications, data management (admin), feedback handling, and communication between stakeholders. The goals are functional and strategic (answering 'why' and 'what' at a high level) without diving into technical implementation details. There are no contradictions or significant omissions regarding the described features.
baselineCritiques.lowLevelGoals: The low-level goals are well-structured, functional, and align closely with the high-level goals and software description. They correctly decompose the high-level objectives into specific actions for each actor (End User, Administrator, Facility Representative). However, there is a minor omission regarding the "data security" aspect mentioned in the description and implied in the Administrator's high-level goals (though the specific HL goal text provided focuses on data accuracy and communication). While security is often a non-functional requirement, the description explicitly mentions "ensuring data security" as a key feature for administrators. A low-level goal such as "Manage user access permissions" or "Audit access logs" could be added to fully represent the system's capabilities as described. Additionally, the End User's ability to "manage" recycling facilities (as per the description "discover and manage") is interpreted as managing their own view/notifications, which is reasonable, but if "manage" implies submitting feedback, that is covered under the Administrator's feedback management (implying users submit it, though the submission action by the End User is missing from the End User's low-level goals). The End User should have a goal to "Submit feedback about a facility."
